done.358: 3. Costs and what is actually received
done.362:
Each transaction has four cost components: spot fee 10 bps, spot slippage 5 bps, perp fee
5 bps, perp slippage 5 bps. Total 25 bps per direction on notional, so 50 bps round-trip.
done.440:
With one transaction, costs are barely noticeable. The problem appears when the strategy
frequently enters and exits: 48 transactions consume about 1,2% of capital, and that is one-third of the profit
over three years.

done.1060:
Negative basis means the perpetual is trading cheaper than spot on entry
and exit, so carry has to bear that difference. A basis of just 20 bps already cuts
nearly half the profit.
done.1070:
With a notional of 0.5x capital, the perpetual short runs at 1x leverage: margin equal to
notional, liquidation only occurs if the price rises by around 100% without additional margin. That
is why its drawdown looks small. But the consequence is that the return is also small.
done.1168:
Historical rally: BTC once rose +60% in 30 days, ETH +70%, SOL +120%. At a notional
of 0.75x, a rally like that would already pass the liquidation point if margin is not added from the spot
leg. Delta-neutral does not mean risk-free; the risk moves to operations.
done.1288:
A more honest comparator for carry is not BTC, but deposits or short-term
debt securities. If risk-free instruments yield 4 to 5% per year, a carry of 3.8%
before tax and operational costs is not worth doing.
